stem:
A 5-year-old boy who recently immigrated to the United States with his family is brought to the office for clumsiness while playing.  The mother's pregnancy was uneventful, but cesarean delivery was required due to obstructed labor.  The mother reports that the patient reached developmental milestones later than his brother.  She has also noticed that the patient's head is large compared to other children of the same age.  Weight is at the 60th percentile for age, height is at the 50th percentile, and head circumference is at the 95th percentile.  MRI of the brain is shown below.

Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​
explanation:
This patient has developmental delay and an enlarged head circumference, prompting evaluation with MRI of the brain.  Imaging reveals hypoplasia/absence of the cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle with posterior fossa enlargement.  These findings are consistent with Dandy-Walker malformation (DWM).

DWM results from a malformation of the cerebellar vermis and the fourth ventricle, which arise from the metencephalon during embryonic development; it may also be associated with other midline deficits (eg, agenesis of corpus callosum, cleft palate).  The malformation leads to atresia of the foramina of Luschka and Magendie.  This results in obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid flow (ie, noncommunicating hydrocephalus) that creates cystic dilation proximal to the level of the obstruction that manifests as enlargement of the posterior fossa extending to the fourth ventricle.

Cerebellar dysfunction can result in unsteadiness and impaired muscle coordination (eg, clumsiness), causing children to have mild to severe developmental delay.  Patients may also exhibit macrocephaly (ie, from progressive enlargement of the head) and symptoms of elevated intracranial pressure (eg, irritability, vomiting).

(Choice A)  Arnold-Chiari malformation, also known as Chiari II malformation, is characterized by downward displacement of the medulla and cerebellar tonsils and vermis below the foramen magnum.  Patients also frequently have spinal myelomeningocele.

(Choice B)  Brain arteriovenous malformation is a developmental vascular lesion that usually presents at age 10-30 with intracranial hemorrhage, seizure, headache, or focal neurologic deficits.

(Choice D)  Encephalocele is a rare neural tube defect characterized by protrusion of the brain and meninges through an abnormal opening in the skull.

(Choice E)  Hypoxic-ischemic brain injury may occur with a complicated delivery (eg, emergency cesarean), but it typically presents with altered consciousness and decreased spontaneous movements during the neonatal period.  Neuroimaging classically shows watershed necrosis of the gray matter between perfusion zones of the major cerebral arteries.

Educational objective:Dandy-Walker malformation is a congenital anomaly characterized by hypoplasia/absence of the cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle with posterior fossa enlargement.  It often presents during infancy with developmental delay and macrocephaly (due to noncommunicating hydrocephalus).​‌​‌​‌​​‌​​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​​‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​‌​​​​‌​​‌‌​‌‌​​​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌​​​​​​‌​‌​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​​​​​‌‌​​​​‌‌​​​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​​​​‌​‌​‌​​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​‌​​​​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌​​​​‌​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌​‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌​‌​‌​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌​‌‌​‌‌​​‌​​​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​
